decisions.mark: identifies ctypes over librentropic.so as the mechanism, with no compiled extension module involved
states that the bindings are GENERATED from the C header by scripts/gen_bindings.py, not hand-written
identifies that drift between the header and the bindings is caught by a pre-commit check that re-runs the generator and diffs
explains that the generated surface is SPLIT IN TWO on purpose — a names-only manifest that imports no ctypes, and the real bindings module that loads the library
concludes that the split exists so `import entropic` succeeds before the engine is on disk, which is what makes an install-engine subcommand shippable inside the same package
describes the loader's resolution order as environment overrides first, then a default user directory, then the system library cache — with two directory layouts tried per root
states the engine-to-caller rule: a returned char* transfers ownership and is freed with entropic_free, while a const char* stays owned by the handle and is only valid until the next call on it
states the caller-to-engine rule as the SECOND direction: a buffer the engine will free must be allocated with entropic_alloc, and shows where the Python side does that
notes that the hook trampoline swallows every Python exception rather than letting it unwind into the C engine, treating a failed hook as a pass-through
